summary.title: You're using a suspiciously old browser
summary.one_liner: This is a notice explaining why the blog's anti-crawler blocks some old browser User-Agent strings, and what visitors can do about it.
keywords: why am i seeing a browser version error
takeaways: The blog blocks requests with old browser User-Agent strings (mostly old Chrome) as part of anti-crawler measures added in early 2025.
Visitors with a current browser who see this page can contact the author with their exact User-Agent string.
Vivaldi users may need to change the 'User Agent Brand Masking' setting so Vivaldi identifies itself instead of Google Chrome.
Some feed readers (Feedly, and possibly Inoreader) may receive this page because they fetch with old browser User-Agents; the author says the problem lies with those services.
archive.today/archive.ph crawlers are hard to tell apart from malicious actors, so the author suggests archive.org instead.
summary.summary: This is a blog notice from Chris Siebenmann shown to visitors whose browser User-Agent is considered too old by the site's anti-crawler rules. It explains that a wave of crawlers using old Chrome User-Agents, possibly for LLM training data, prompted the blocking. It also covers why feed readers like Feedly and Inoreader may see the page, why Vivaldi users may need to change a brand-masking setting, and why archive.today crawls are blocked and archive.org is recommended. The page is a short first-person notice rather than a technical tutorial.
